Explain the example for line up a row with flex

blocks.text: Flex layout places child boxes in a row by default. You can centre them vertically and give them a gap.

These examples use Tailwind CSS 4 in a separate project. Install tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/cli. Put @import "tailwindcss"; in input.css and build with npx @tailwindcss/cli -i input.css -o output.css. Link output.css in HTML.

blocks.title: Line up a row with flex

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `items-center` aligns flex items on the cross axis. In a row, that usually aligns their vertical centres.
`gap-3` adds space between layout items without adding outer margins around the whole group.

blocks.text: The label and count sit in a row, aligned through the middle, with space between them.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: items-center aligns across the row. It does not put all the items into the centre of the page.

blocks.text: Add one more span and watch how the row changes.
